questions.question: What is the main advantage of OKLCH over HSL for building a colour palette?
options: OKLCH colours are always inside the sRGB gamut
OKLCH uses hexadecimal values, which are shorter
OKLCH lightness is perceptual, so colours with the same L look about equally light, making contrast predictable
OKLCH supports transparency and HSL does not
questions.explanation: HSL lightness ignores how the eye perceives different hues. OKLCH's L channel is perceptual and it can also describe wide-gamut colours beyond sRGB.

questions.question: What does `oklch(from var(--brand) calc(l - 0.08) c h)` produce?
options: A colour with the same chroma and hue as --brand but slightly darker
An error, because calc() cannot be used inside colour functions
questions.explanation: Relative colour syntax destructures the origin colour into l, c and h, and here reduces the lightness channel while keeping the others.

questions.question: With `color-scheme: light dark` on `:root` and `--surface: light-dark(white, black)`, how do you build a manual dark-mode toggle?
options: Duplicate every token inside a [data-theme="dark"] block
Use JavaScript to rewrite every light-dark() call
light-dark() only follows the operating system and cannot be overridden
Set color-scheme: dark on the root when the user picks dark; light-dark() then resolves to its second value
questions.explanation: light-dark() responds to the element's used colour scheme, so changing color-scheme is enough to flip every token.

questions.question: Why would you register a custom property with `@property` and `syntax: "<angle>"`?
options: So it can be used outside of :root
So the browser knows its type and can interpolate it in transitions and animations
So it becomes available to Sass at build time
questions.explanation: Unregistered custom properties are untyped and jump between values. A typed registration lets the browser animate them smoothly and gives an initial-value fallback.
